title: Austin's New Cemetery Rules & Tax Penalties
summary:
*   Comprehensive new rules were adopted for Oakwood Cemetery, dictating everything from grave decorations and plot transfers to visitor conduct and funeral procedures.
*   A new ordinance passed, establishing a 5% penalty for delinquent municipal tax payments.
*   Half of a fine for public intoxication was remitted for a citizen named Buster Anderson.
*   The City formally documented a long list of refunding bonds from 1901 that had recently been destroyed by burning.

Cemetery rules for Oakwood Annex.
1. All lots shall be held and used in accordance with the ordinances of the City of Austin
and the bylaws and rules and regulations of Oakwood Cemetery and of Oakwood Annex now in
force or hereafter adopted ,and lots shall not be used for any purpose than the burial of
the human dead.
2. Lot holders shall not allow interments to be made upon their lots for a compensation;
nor shall any transfer or assignment of any lot or interest therein be valid without the
consent of the Mayor of the City of Austin first had and endorsed upon UNXMM such transfer
or assignment and duly entered of record by the City Assessor & Collector of this City.
3. The corners of each lot will be permanently marked by the City of Austin.
4. No lot or parcel of ground shall be defined by any fence, railing, coping, hedge,
embankment or ditch ,nor shall any seat ,rock-work or wire-work or any architectural
object be erected ,except as hereinafter specified.
5. No lot or grave shall be decorated by its owner, or others interested therein, with any
tree, shrub, flower or plant, or the trees or scrubs disturbed in any way without first
obtaining the consent of the Supt of Parks and Public property. This does not ,however,
include the placing of cut flowers on the graves.
6. No lot shall be filled above the established grade ,nor shall any construction be
allowed which will interfere with the proper care of the lawns.
7. Mounds above graves shall not exceed in height two and one-half inches ,when thoroughly
settled.
8. No advertisement of any kind whatever will be permitted within the cemetery.
9. The City of Austin reserves the right to remove from any lot anything that conflicts
with therules and regulations.
10. The Supt of Parks and Public Property, through the Cemetery Sexton, has entire charge
of the cemetery and he is authorized to enforce all rules, to maintain order, to overlook
all workmen ,visitors and drivers and to expell those who disregard his orders. He is
further authorized to inspect and refuse entrance to any and all materialswhen necessary,
and to insist on the immediate removal of all trash and building material as soon as
buildings or .

11. The City of Austin shall perpetually care for and maintain all roads,paths, vegetation
and lots and grounds and all improvements and shrubbery,but the lot owners must care for
and maintainall tablets,monuments or vaults erected on their lots.
12. All charges for interments ,graves,grading,excavations for vaults and other cemetery
expenses must be paid for in advance. Monuments.
13. No monument or head tablet or other structure shall be placed upon any lot until a
design of the same has been submitted and accepted and the location thereof on the lot
approved by the Supt of Parks and Public Property.All work of whatever nature ,except the
erection of monuments and head tablets,shall be done by the employees of the cemetery and
under the direct supervision of the Supt of Parks and Public Property,or his
representative.
Funerals and interments.
14. When a burial is required,notice thereof,together with a permit from the City Health
Officer,must be given to the Supt of Parks and Public Property,or his representative, at
least four hours before the interment.
The City in cases of burial,will require a record of the following particu-lars: Name of
deceased,place of birth, date of birth,date of deceased,last res-idence,cause of
death,name of nearest living relative and name of Undertaker This record will be tabulated
and placed in the vaults of the City and will constitute a permanent record.
15. Any lot holder has the right to give permission by written order for the burial of the
remains of others than his immediate family,but not for remuneration.
16. One interment only may be made in each grave.
17. Undertakers, drivers and all others employed at funerals are under the control and
subject to the direction of the Supt of Parks and Public Property,or of the City Sexton,or
his assistants. Receiving Tomb.
18. Bodies may be placed in the receiving tomb at all times,but the period during which
they may be permitted to remain shall not exceed two months.The City of Austin reserves
the right of interment or removal whenever it may appear necessary ,after forty eight
hours notice to friend 19. When a body is to be deposited in the tomb,a permit, as in case
of an interment ,must be obtained from the City Health Officer.
20.The remains of any person dying from any contagious disease will not be permitted in
the receiving tomb.
21. Before the deposit of any body in the receiving tomb there shall be paid to the City
Treasurer for each body so deposited the sum of ten (10.00) dollars. If removed within one
month there will be allowed $5.00, and if a family lot is purchased within fifteen days
,there will be allow-ed $ 10.00 on the purchase price of lot and burial.Lot owners are
only required to pay a fee of $ 5.00 for the use of the receiving tomb.

Visitors.
22.Gates are open at all reasonable hours for visitors.
23. All persons are prohibited from gathering flowers or breaking any tree,shrub or
plant,or writing upon or defacing any monument,fence or other structure,in or belonging to
the cemetery.
24. No person will be permitted to bring refreshments into the cemetery,and no firearms
orother assemblies other than funeral will be allowed.
25. No fast driving will be allowed within the grounds and horses must not be left
unattended within the cemetery and no hitching ai permitted.
26. Persons accompanied by dogs ,or carrying fire arms will not be admitted to the
cemetery.Traffic vehicles and omnibuses will not be admitted.
27. Visitors are reminded that the grounds are sacredly devoted to the interment of the
dead,and a strict observance of proper decorum will be required of all.The Officers and
agents of the City are authorized and directed to remove all persons who may commit any
indecorum or violate any of the rules. ✔ fixing date of The Mayor laid before the Council

ordinances and parts of ordinances in conflict herewith, which ordinance was read the
first time on the 17th day of January 1918,and laid over.
The ordinance was read the second time,and passed under suspension of the rule,by the
following vote: Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5
